title: Narasimha
hook: a boy won't stop saying one name, and his father wants him to
tomorrow: is Vishnu in the pillar? the king is about to find out.

segments.voice: Yesterday, Varaha: Vishnu as the boar, lifting the earth up out of the waters. In the Bhagavata, the demon he fought, Hiranyaksha, had a brother. That brother never forgot.

Some kids come home and announce what they learned at school whether anyone asked or not. This one gets asked. A king lifts his small son onto his lap and says: tell me the best thing your teachers have taught you. And the boy, Prahlada, answers without blinking. The best thing is to remember Vishnu. The king goes cold. Vishnu is the god who killed his brother. The teachers swear they never taught the boy that. Prahlada says nobody had to.
screen: `TELL ME THE BEST THING YOU LEARNED.` → `REMEMBER VISHNU.` → `NOBODY HAD TO TEACH HIM.`

segments.voice: The king is Hiranyakashipu, and in the Bhagavata Purana he has made himself nearly impossible to kill. His kingdom has one rule: no one worships Vishnu. His own son breaks it, cheerfully, out loud. So the king tries to get rid of the problem. In the telling, Prahlada is thrown before elephants, given to snakes, fed poison, dropped from a height, and each time he comes through. But here's the part worth telling a friend tonight. In between all that, the boy goes back to school, and when the teachers step out, he teaches the other children. They're the sons of demons, raised to fight the gods. And Prahlada tells them: the Lord lives in every being, in you, in me, in anyone you'd call an enemy. Dividing the world into mine and not mine, friend and enemy, comes from a confused mind. So be a friend to every creature. Then he goes further: being born a god, a sage or into a fine family isn't what counts. Anyone at all can turn toward the Lord. A child in a demon's palace, saying the circle has no outside. Then the king calls him in one more time and points at a stone pillar in the hall. If your Vishnu is everywhere, he says, is he in this?
screen: `ONE RULE: NO VISHNU.` · `HE COMES THROUGH, EVERY TIME.` · `RECESS: THE LORD IS IN EVERYONE.` · `BIRTH ISN'T WHAT COUNTS.` · then, large: `IS HE IN THIS PILLAR?`

segments.voice: Pick one sound around you, a fridge humming, traffic, a bird, your own breath, and stay with just that sound for the sit. When your mind wanders off to judge it, nice or annoying, come back to simply hearing it. One steady thing to listen for, the way Prahlada kept one name.
Narasimha: Vishnu as the man-lion, from nara, man, and simha, lion. He hasn't arrived yet. Prahlada is still standing by the pillar.
Hold on to it: Narasimha, and a child in a demon's palace who said the Lord lives in everyone. Back tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1541 COUNTS.` → `THE PURANAS · 31 OF 56.` → `TOMORROW: IS VISHNU IN THE PILLAR?`

howItsDone: In some Hindu families Prahlada's story is retold around Holi, and Narasimha Jayanti marks the evening the man-lion appeared; children often meet Prahlada as the boy who would not stop remembering Vishnu.

fork.setup: your friends tease you for a small habit you keep: a thank-you before meals, a page you read each night. by Prahlada's story, what fits?

original.note: Sanskrit: nara, man, plus simha, lion. The man-lion form of Vishnu.

notes: Story shape. Narasimha run, day 1 of 4 (1541–1544): Prahlada and the pillar question; 1542 the boon and its loopholes; 1543 the boon Prahlada refuses (debate); 1544 the hand on his head and his wish for his father. 1537–1540 were not on disk when this was written; the review assumes 1540 told Varaha and Hiranyaksha (Bhagavata 3.18–19; 7.2 names Hiranyaksha as Hiranyakashipu's brother). Confirm against 1540.

Confirm in Bhagavata 7.5: Prahlada's answer on his father's lap (hearing and remembering Vishnu as the best thing learned); the teachers' denial; the attempts (elephants, snakes, poison, being thrown from a height). 7.5.11–12: 'mine and not mine', friend and enemy, from a confused mind. 7.6.24: friendship or compassion toward all beings. 7.7.51–52: birth as a god, sage or brahmin is not what pleases the Lord. All paraphrased.
For parents: the attempts on a child's life are one plain sentence with no detail.
nara + simha is the plain reading of the name; confirm under the claims rule.
howItsDone: Holi and Holika are not in the Bhagavata; hedged 'in some Hindu families'. Confirm or cut. 'often' in the last clause: soften if needed.
Surprising fact: at school, a demon king's son teaches the demon boys that the Lord lives in every being (Bhagavata 7.6–7.7).
Unity thread, inside the tradition: 'the circle has no outside' (the Lord in every being; birth isn't what counts). No other tradition named today.
